name: Qualified Piper
tagline: An AI SDR agent that works your website traffic, identifies visitors, chats them up, and books meetings into Salesforce.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Qualified sells through sales with annual contracts, Piper is typically quoted on top.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely build a website chat widget with an LLM behind it in one sitting, and it will feel impressive for about ten minutes. What you cannot build is the part Qualified actually sells: knowing that the anonymous visitor on your pricing page is a director at a 4,000 person company in an active buying cycle, and writing that into Salesforce in a way a sales team trusts. That identification comes from purchased IP-to-company and intent datasets plus years of firmographic plumbing, and the Salesforce-native data model is the reason it survives procurement. Also worth saying plainly: this is a tool for a revenue team with inbound traffic and a CRM, not a personal app, so there is no personal replacement to want. Build the chat toy if you enjoy it, do not pretend it replaces this.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted chat widget on your own site that an LLM answers from your docs, qualifies with a few scripted questions, and drops a booking link plus a transcript into a local database.
requirements: your own site to embed a script tag on
a public URL for the widget backend
a calendar booking link you already have
whatYouLose: Visitor identification: no IP-to-company, no firmographics, no intent signals, so every conversation starts anonymous
Salesforce-native objects, routing rules, and attribution that sales ops actually reports on
Live handoff to a human rep with presence, routing, and voice/screen share in the same session
Meeting booking that respects real rep calendars, territories, and round robin
Any audit trail, SOC 2 posture, or data processing paperwork your legal team will ask about
moatNotes: The chat UI is the thinnest part of the product. The expensive parts are the identity graph underneath and the Salesforce object model on top.
whyPeopleStillPay: Companies pay because inbound traffic is the most expensive traffic they have and leaving it to a contact form is measurable money lost. Qualified sits in the one place where marketing spend turns into pipeline, speaks fluent Salesforce so the numbers show up where the CRO already looks, and tells a rep who the visitor is before the rep says hello. Replacing that means replacing the data vendors, the CRM integration, and the internal trust that the pipeline numbers are real. A self-hosted chatbot replaces none of those three.
notes: The chat widget is an afternoon; the thing it whispers to the rep is not. The moat is bought identity data welded to a Salesforce-native object model that revenue teams already report against.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted website chat agent I can embed on my own site. This is a personal/small-site tool, not a sales platform.

Stack, no substitutions:
- TypeScript, Node 20, Fastify for the backend
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage, single file at ./data/chat.db
- A single vanilla JS widget bundle served from the same server, embedded with one script tag, no React
- OpenAI API for responses, key from .env as OPENAI_API_KEY

In scope:
1. POST /api/chat accepts { sessionId, message } and streams a reply via server-sent events.
2. Answer from a local knowledge base: read every .md file in ./knowledge at boot, chunk it, embed it once, cache embeddings in SQLite, retrieve top 5 chunks per turn. Re-embed only when a file hash changes.
3. System prompt lives in ./config/agent.md so I can edit tone and qualifying questions without touching code.
4. After 3 user turns, the agent may offer a booking link read from BOOKING_URL in .env. Never invent a link.
5. Persist every session: id, created_at, page_url, referrer, user_agent, full transcript as JSON, and a boolean flag for whether the booking link was shown.
6. GET /admin (protected by ADMIN_TOKEN in .env, simple bearer check) renders a plain server-side HTML list of sessions with transcripts, newest first, plus a CSV export endpoint.
7. The widget: bubble bottom right, opens a panel, remembers sessionId in localStorage, works on mobile, no external fonts or CDNs.
8. Rate limit by IP: 30 messages per hour, return a polite refusal past that.

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt or stub:
- Visitor identification, IP-to-company lookup, firmographic or intent enrichment
- Any CRM sync, Salesforce objects, or lead routing
- Human rep handoff, presence, voice, or screen share
- Analytics pixels, telemetry, or third-party trackers of any kind

Deliver: README with setup in under 10 steps, .env.example, a seed ./knowledge/example.md, and one script `npm run dev` that serves both API and widget on port 8787.
